messages:
Maya Chen: heads-up — noticed a cluster of premium tenants getting routed to eu-west with the 8-bit quantized variant during the outage window yesterday. their latency probe scores dipped briefly but our current probe logic flips immediately. leads to visible degradation for them. anyone up for smoothing/probe hysteresis ideas?
Sam Ortiz: ugh saw that in the dashboard. probes are noisy for short spikes. we should probably add a weighted moving average + min-sample window before switching region. also expose the probe metric to console (per-tenant) so support can see it.
Kevin Patel: agree on smoothing. we should also tie routing behavior to customer tier. premium = stricter acceptance threshold and slower decay (longer hysteresis). free = more aggressive failover to keep cost down.
Maya Chen: exactly. current rule is identical for all tiers which is dumb. proposal: add two knobs on routing policy: `probe_lookback_secs` and `probe_decay_multiplier_by_tier`. default for premium: lookback 30s, decay_mult 0.5. for free: lookback 8s, decay_mult 1.2.
Lucy Tran: quick UX ask — can we show both the raw probe ping series and the smoothed score on per-route dashboards? support needs to know if it's a brief blip or sustained failure. small sparkline + last-sample ts should suffice.
Sam Ortiz: yes, will add to console. also add a small note: "smoothed score uses EWMA alpha configurable per-tenant".
Kevin Patel: another angle: model variant fanout. when a premium request is at risk, instead of one-off fallback to quantized model in a different region, we can try parallel fanout to up to 2 variants: primary-region/full-precision + standby-region/quantized. accept-first-winner. that keeps latency bounded but increases cost. policy should be tier-gated.
Maya Chen: love that. but need to prevent amplification under high load. maybe: parallel-fanout allowed only when tenant_qps < fanout_qps_threshold AND cost_budget_flag for tenant is true. otherwise sequential fallback.
Rajiv Singh: careful about oscillation — parallel fanout can mask the real health signal if we keep succeeding via standby. we should tag those requests in telemetry (route_decision = "parallel_fanout") and decrement probe weight for the standby path so it doesn't artificially inflate standby health. Also cooldown windows after region switch (e.g., 2m) to avoid flip-flops.
Kevin Patel: good call. add `last_switch_ts` and enforce `min_switch_interval`. also include a small backoff multiplier on probe score updates after a switch: `probe_suppress_secs`.
Maya Chen: putting a sample config here for the routing policy I sketched:
```
routing_policy:
  tiers:
    premium:
      probe_lookback_secs: 30
      ewma_alpha: 0.25
      probe_decay_multiplier: 0.5
      allow_parallel_fanout: true
      fanout_qps_threshold: 5
      min_switch_interval_secs: 120
      probe_suppress_secs: 20
    standard:
      probe_lookback_secs: 15
      ewma_alpha: 0.4
      probe_decay_multiplier: 0.9
      allow_parallel_fanout: false
      fanout_qps_threshold: 2
      min_switch_interval_secs: 60
      probe_suppress_secs: 10
```
Sam Ortiz: looks good. for the API, propose `/v1/routing/evaluate?tenant=...&model=...` that returns the decision and the factors (scores, last_switch, tier). that helps support + e2e tests.
Lucy Tran: we'll need telemetry fields: `routing_decision`, `probe_raw`, `probe_smoothed`, `variant_attempts`, `fanout_used`, `cost_estimate`. add those to ingestion pipeline.
OpsBot: deploy triggered by Maya Chen: routing-policy/feature/ewma-hysteresis -> staging at 2024-09-15T16:42:12Z :rocket:
Maya Chen: FYI QA will run a canary that simulates short spikes and sustained region latency. please watch the canary metrics.
Rajiv Singh: one more operational note — quota accounting when parallel fanout happens. we need to ensure billing/usage shows the effective token amplification (two model calls) so internal cost attribution is accurate. finance asked for that after the last incident.
Lucy Tran: noted. console should surface both effective tokens and raw tokens by variant.
Sam Ortiz: i'll draft the API and telemetry PRs today. @Kevin @Maya can you review the routing config changes?
Kevin Patel: will review tonight.
Maya Chen: thanks all. follow-ups: Sam to add API + telemetry schema, Kevin to review config, Lucy to wire console sparkline, Rajiv to add cooldown tests. i'll coordinate canary window. :thumbsup:
